sections.label: Proposed changes in two areas
sections.summary: It proposes changes in enforcement of maintenance orders and in Court proceedings and procedure in the Family Justice Courts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Conceptually, it proposes changes in two areas: one, on the enforcement of maintenance orders; and two, on Court proceedings and procedure in the Family Justice Courts (FJC).

sections.label: Singapore's Therapeutic Justice approach
sections.summary: Singapore has taken a modified approach to family disputes focusing on Therapeutic Justice, which tries to get parties to reach common ground and move on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you apply that kind of approach to family disputes, I think the tendency will often be to deepen the rift between the parties and it could overlook the well-being of the children who are caught in the middle.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, in Singapore, for some time now, we have taken a modified approach to family disputes, focusing on Therapeutic Justice.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The approach tries to get the parties to reach a common ground and move on with their lives.

sections.label: Maintenance enforcement applications 2017-2019
sections.summary: Before COVID-19, from 2017 to 2019, there was an annual average of 2,700 applications to enforce maintenance orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Before COVID-19, from 2017 to 2019, there was an annual average of 2,700 applications to enforce maintenance orders.

sections.label: Child maintenance arrears by 2022
sections.summary: By 2022, child maintenance arrears accumulated over 61 months totalled $91,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: By 2022, the child maintenance arrears, accumulated over 61 months, was a total of $91,000.

sections.label: White Paper on Women's Development
sections.summary: The 2021 White Paper on Women's Development recognised maintenance enforcement as a key challenge and committed to simplify and strengthen enforcement and minimise repeat applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In the White Paper on Women’s Development, which was issued in 2021, the Government recognised maintenance enforcement as a key challenge for women in vulnerable situations, and the Government committed to simplify and strengthen the enforcement process and minimise the need for repeat applications for enforcement.

sections.label: Functions of appointed MEOs
sections.summary: MEOs, appointed by the Law Minister, can conduct fact-finding, refer needy parties to support, conduct conciliation sessions, and submit gathered information to the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: MEOs will be appointed by the Law Minister and their functions will include the following: one, they can conduct fact-finding on the parties’ financial circumstances; two, they can refer suitable and needy parties to financial assistance and other forms of support; three, they can conduct conciliation sessions and facilitate settlements between the parties; four, they can submit the information gathered from the fact-finding and conciliation sessions to the Court.

sections.label: MEO seeking information from parties
sections.summary: If information is insufficient, the MEO may seek information from parties, banks and prescribed third parties including CPF, HDB, IRAS, SLA, LTA and CDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the information is insufficient, the MEO may seek information from the parties, banks, third parties, some of whom will be prescribed and these would include Central Provident Fund (CPF), Housing and Development Board (HDB), Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS), Singapore Land Authority (SLA), Land Transport Authority (LTA) and the Central Depository (Pte) Limited (CDP).

sections.label: SPO period and payments
sections.summary: The SPO will usually last six months and require the respondent to show the Court at specified intervals that requisite payments were made.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The SPO will usually be for a period of six months and it will require the respondent to show to the Court, at specified future intervals, that he or she has made the requisite payments.

sections.label: Three aims of amendments
sections.summary: The three aims are stronger deterrence against non-compliance, more sustainable maintenance outcomes for families in financial difficulty, and easier enforcement of maintenance orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Primarily, three things: one, stronger deterrence against non-compliance with maintenance orders; two, more sustainable maintenance outcomes for families with genuine financial difficulties; and three, easier process for enforcement of maintenance orders when they are not complied with.

sections.label: Withholding access and MEP
sections.summary: An applicant with care and control may withhold access if maintenance is late, and the MEP aims to make the post-divorce journey slightly easier.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, an applicant with care and control of the children may be tempted to withhold access to them, if the respondent does not make timely maintenance payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: These disputes that linger and spiral long after the divorce proceedings can worsen the anguish for the parties and their children and also take a toll on those around them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: With the MEP, we hope to change a bit of this and make the post-divorce journey slightly easier.

sections.label: Effects of the amendments
sections.summary: The amendments strengthen protection for children and vulnerable parties, make family proceedings simpler and more efficient, and strengthen Therapeutic Justice elements in FJC proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The amendments will: strengthen protection for children and other vulnerable parties, including victims of family violence; make family proceedings simpler and more efficient, thereby enhancing access to justice for all Court users of the FJC; strengthen Therapeutic Justice elements in FJC proceedings, by giving the Courts the power to manage proceedings in a manner which reduces acrimony and ensures a fair outcome without undue delay, complexity and cost.

sections.label: Women's Charter 2022 access orders
sections.summary: The Women's Charter was amended in 2022 to let the Court order additional access, compensation for expenses, and counselling, mediation, therapeutic or educational programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Women's Charter was amended in 2022 to empower the Court to make orders to grant the access parent additional access to the child to make up for the access denied; for the care and control parent to compensate the access parent for expenses incurred as a result of the breach of the child access order; and both parties and the child, or any of them, to attend counselling, mediation, therapeutic or educational programmes.

sections.label: Section 11A variation applications orders
sections.summary: Section 11A lets the FJC bar or expunge meritless variation applications affecting a child's welfare or based on past conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Section 11A provides that where (a) the filing of any variation application or supporting document, or (b) any variation application or supporting document which has been filed by a party, will or is likely to be without merit, having regard to the applicant's past conduct in previous proceedings or has an adverse effect on the welfare of a child, FJC may make, among other things, the following orders: (a)	an order prohibiting the filing of the variation application or other variation application, or any document in support of such applications, without the permission of the Court; and (b)	an order that any variation application or any supporting document which has been filed be treated as dismissed or expunged on a specified date, unless the party complies with one or more conditions imposed by the Court by that date.

sections.label: Section 11A interlocutory applications orders
sections.summary: Section 11A lets the FJC bar or expunge interlocutory applications that impede resolution or harm a child's welfare.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Section 11A provides that where (a) the filing of any interlocutory application or supporting document, or (b) any interlocutory application or supporting document which has been filed, will, or is likely to: impede the just, expeditious or economical resolution or disposal of the matter; or have an adverse effect on the child's welfare, the FJC may make, among other things, the following orders: (a)	an order prohibiting the filing of the interlocutory application or any other interlocutory application, or any document in support of such applications, without the permission of the Court; and (b)	an order that any interlocutory application or any supporting document which has been filed be treated as dismissed or expunged on a specified date, unless the party complies with one or more conditions imposed by the Court by that date.

sections.label: Section 11A applied to Ms C
sections.summary: The Court could bar the mother from filing further revocation applications without permission if they are without merit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Applying the new section 11A to Ms C's situation, the Court will be empowered to make an order prohibiting the mother from filing any further applications to revoke the protection orders in favour of Ms C, her father and her sibling without the Court's permission, if the Court is satisfied that the filing of any application to revoke the protection orders will be without merit, having regard to the mother's conduct in past proceedings, including the mother's series of unmeritorious applications to revoke the protection orders in the past.

sections.label: New section 11B
sections.summary: The new section 11B of the Family Justice Act will implement the Committee's recommendation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The new section 11B of the Family Justice Act will implement the Committee's recommendation.

sections.label: New section 11C cross-examination
sections.summary: Section 11C empowers the FJC to restrict the scope, duration or manner of cross-examination of a witness.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The second key provision is the new section 11C of the Family Justice Act, which will empower FJC to, on its own motion, or upon the application of any party, make the following orders: an order that cross-examination of a witness be restricted in scope or duration and an order that cross-examination be conducted in any manner prescribed by the FJR.

sections.label: Section 11C circumstances and child's wishes
sections.summary: Section 11C limits such orders to prescribed circumstances, and the Bill lets the FJR set modes for determining a child's wishes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The new section 11C, therefore, provides that the Court may only make the orders restricting cross-examination in circumstances to be prescribed in the FJR, for example, in circumstances where the questioning of a vulnerable witness is or is likely to be unduly intimidating and oppressive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The third key provision in the Bill provides that the FJR may set out the modes by which the wishes of a child may be determined by the Court.

sections.label: Family Court powers and judgments
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies Family Court and Youth Court powers, appointment of officers for mediation, and lump sum, instalment, suspended or stayed judgment orders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Bill will clarify in the Family Justice Act that a Family Court or Youth Court has such powers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Bill will also clarify in legislation the existing powers of the Court to appoint Judicial officers, officers of the FJC or any other persons, such as volunteer lawyers, to conduct mediations or other ADR processes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Second, the Bill will adopt section 43 of the State Courts Act which applies to a District Court, by expressly providing that the Family Court may order that a judgment sum be paid in a lump sum or by instalments, and may order that a judgment be suspended or stayed if the judgment debtor is unable to pay the sum.

sections.label: Post-divorce family arrangements
sections.summary: The amendments aim to help divorcees make post-divorce family arrangements, with about 2,700 maintenance enforcement applications yearly from 2017 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   The aim of the amendments is to enable divorcees to better make post-divorce arrangements for the family.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We have seen an average of 2,700 maintenance enforcement applications annually across the years 2017 to 2019.

sections.label: New Maintenance Enforcement Process
sections.summary: The amendments introduce a Maintenance Enforcement Process empowering the Maintenance Enforcement Officer to request financial information from Government agencies, banks and other agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The amendments, therefore, introduce a new Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Under this new process, the Maintenance Enforcement Officer (MEO) will be empowered to ensure more sustainable maintenance outcomes: first, the MEO will be empowered to request for information on the respondent’s financial situation from Government agencies, banks and other agencies.

sections.label: Maintenance orders and Women's Charter amendments
sections.summary: The Court can vary maintenance orders based on financial situation, a rebuttable presumption on dissipated assets is introduced, and Women's Charter amendments cover CPP, divorce by mutual agreement and child access enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: For respondents who face difficulties in making their maintenance payments, under certain circumstances, the Court can vary the original maintenance order based on their actual financial situation, without requiring the respondent to submit a formal application.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces a rebuttable presumption, that is to say, under certain circumstances, as long as the respondent has dissipated their assets, it will be presumed that the respondent has done so with the intention of frustrating the maintenance order.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Women’s Charter included the extension of the mandatory CPP to all divorcing parents with minor children to better support parents in making informed decisions regarding their divorce that prioritise the well-being of their children, the introduction of the Divorce by Mutual Agreement of the Irretrievable Breakdown of the Marriage to reduce acrimony in the divorce process, and the introduction of a new suite of measures for the enforcement of child access.

sections.label: Court orders on own motion
sections.summary: Clause 4 proposes giving the Court power to make orders on its own motion after affected persons are heard, and to impose cross-examination restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, I note that it is proposed in clause 4 of the Bill that the Court be given powers to make an order on its own motion, without application by the parties, so long as every person likely to be affected by the Court's order is given an opportunity to be heard beforehand; and impose restrictions during cross-examination, as it sees fit.

sections.label: Matrimonial property division and housing
sections.summary: Giving the Court power to act on its own motion helps it decide matrimonial property division justly, minimising hardship cases where parties and children lack suitable housing after HDB flats are sold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: By providing the Court with the power to act on its own motion on substantive matters, it will be in a better position to make a just and equitable decision on the division of matrimonial property that affects the housing arrangements of the parties and their children post-divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, be better able to minimise the number of hardship cases involving parties and their children who run the risk of not having any place to stay or stay in less than conducive environments after they have sold their HDB flats pursuant to a Court order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Also, I wonder if a protocol among the Court, parties and HDB can be established to resolve the information asymmetry that I have highlighted here.

sections.label: MEOs direct information access
sections.summary: MEOs will be able to get information directly from stipulated entities including banks, CDP, CPF Board, HDB, IRAS, LTA and SLA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: MEOs will be able to get directly information from stipulated entities, such as banks, CDP, CPF Board, HDB, IRAS, LTA and SLA.

sections.label: MEO subject to Minister directions
sections.summary: The proposal is that the MEO act subject to the Minister's general or special directions insofar as they are not inconsistent with the Bill's clauses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Here, it is proposed that the MEO act, “subject to the general or special directions of the Minister insofar as the directions are not inconsistent” with the clauses in the Bill under consideration.

sections.label: Bodies provide information, court orders
sections.summary: These bodies may provide information under future regulations, and the MEO may request a Court order for a third party to provide relevant information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: These bodies may provide information as permitted under regulations which will be enacted sometime in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I also note that, apart from the “bank” and a “prescribed third party”, the MEO may request the Court for an order that a “third party” provide him with relevant information.

sections.label: Clarifying officers' independence
sections.summary: The second point seeks clarity on the independence of such officers and how far their work requires arms' length from the Executive arm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My second requires us to clarify a small but not unimportant matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This clarity will help answer questions about the independence of such officers and to what extent their work requires an arms’ length from the Executive arm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is a point that hon Minister of State Sun Xueling made at the outset of her speech when she said that MSF's aim is to nurture families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is important that the legislative process works to protect the interests of all parties when marriages dissolve.

sections.label: New MEP maintenance orders scope
sections.summary: The new MEP will apply to maintenance orders under the Women's Charter, Guardianship of Infants Act, Administration of Muslim Law Act, Maintenance Orders (Reciprocal Enforcement) Act and Maintenance of Parents Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Our laws must provide for this less intimate, but paradoxically, in this context, more enduring connection, in the pursuit of family justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The new MEP will apply to maintenance orders under the Women's Charter, Guardianship of Infants Act, Administration of Muslim Law Act, Maintenance Orders (Reciprocal Enforcement) Act and the Maintenance of Parents Act.

sections.label: Maintenance enforcement application and MEO report
sections.summary: Under clause 89, once a maintenance enforcement application is made, MEOs must prepare and submit a report to the Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Many prefer to spend the time earning more income to make up for their former spouses’ maintenance payments instead of expending time and efforts in applying repeatedly for enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I note that under the new process, if a maintenance order has not been complied with, the applicant will have to make an application, albeit online, and if the Court were to make a Show-Payment Order requiring proof of payment, specifying an imprisonment term for the respondent’s breach of the Show-Payment Order, does that mean that the respondent can pay up after such an application is made for a Show-Payment Order or when he receives such an order?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Next, I note that under clause 89, once a maintenance enforcement application has been made, the MEOs have to prepare and submit a report to the Court.

sections.label: Women not working due to caregiving
sections.summary: MOM's 2022 Labour Force Survey found about a quarter of a million women of economic age are not in the workforce due to caregiving.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM)'s Labour Force Survey in 2022, there are approximately a quarter of a million women of economic age who are not participating in the workforce due to caregiving responsibilities.

sections.label: Emily's case and maintenance enforcement
sections.summary: The speaker says Emily's case is not unique, supports better enforcement of maintenance orders, and calls for a cost-effective, simplified process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Sadly, Emily’s case, or variations of her case, is not unique, and I support the changes of better enforcement of maintenance orders, and I call on the Government, in the execution of the enforcement, a cost-effective and simplified process.

sections.label: CUBack@Work programme for women
sections.summary: The speaker says creative programmes supporting women in transition were launched with unionised companies, the most recent being CUBack@Work or CUB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Indeed, we have launched with our unionised companies many creative programmes that support our women in transition, the most recent being the CUBack@Work, or CUB programme.

sections.label: MEO referral to social service officer
sections.summary: New section 85 of the Family Justice Reform Bill lets the MEO refer and provide information on parties involved to a social service officer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The new section 85 of the Family Justice Reform Bill enables the MEO to refer and provide information regarding the parties involved to a social service officer.

sections.label: Financial assistance for MEO-referred parties
sections.summary: The speaker proposes the Ministry consider extra consideration or a baseline of financial assistance for MEO-referred parties in maintenance enforcement cases, especially with reduced maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would especially hit the children involved and their caregivers hard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I propose that the Ministry consider granting additional consideration for, or even guaranteeing a baseline level of financial assistance to parties referred by the MEO during cases pertaining to the enforcement of a maintenance order, especially if it involves a reduced maintenance amount.

sections.label: Child's voice and divorce issues
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill allows measures ensuring the child's voice is heard, and comments on children's education and housing needs in divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Bill provides us with the opportunity to implement these measures, which would ensure that the child's voice is heard loud and clear, especially pertaining to a matter that affects their lives substantially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Before I conclude, I would also like to make some brief comments on issues outside the ambit of this Bill, relating to the education and housing needs of children involved in a divorce – two of the fundamental rights of a child.

sections.label: Housing for divorced parents
sections.summary: Divorcees with shared care and control of their children have an equal right to list the children when applying to buy or rent an HDB flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: On housing, divorcees with shared care and control of their children have an equal right to list the children in their application to buy or rent an HDB flat.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and hopes the additional suggestions made can be considered to help broken families restart their lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To conclude, I am supportive of this Bill and I hope the additional suggestions I have made can be considered to alleviate the anxiety and anguish inflicted upon the now broken families and enable those involved to better pick themselves up and restart their lives afresh.

sections.label: Stronger enforcement of maintenance orders
sections.summary: The Bill proposes stronger enforcement of maintenance orders, including automatic deduction of maintenance payments from wages, bank accounts or CPF.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: One of the most significant features of this Bill is the stronger enforcement of maintenance orders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes measures, such as the automatic deduction of maintenance payments from the defaulting party's wages, bank accounts or CPF.

sections.label: Penalties for unpaid maintenance
sections.summary: Under the new process, parents who fail to pay maintenance face more stringent enforcement measures, including imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Under the new process, parents who fail to pay maintenance will be subjected to more stringent enforcement measures, including imprisonment.

sections.label: Call for gender-neutral maintenance
sections.summary: The speaker calls for the Government to consider providing for gender-neutral maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Beyond amending the legislation to make it easier to enforce maintenance payments, going forward, I would like to call for the Government to consider providing for gender-neutral maintenance.

sections.label: Wives as sole breadwinners
sections.summary: The Singapore Census Population 2020 showed the percentage of married households where wives are the sole breadwinners rose from 5.8% in 2010 to 7.4% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singapore Census Population 2020 showed that the percentage of married households where wives are the sole breadwinners – and I stress, married households – increased from 5.8% in 2010 to 7.4% in 2020.

sections.label: Dual-income married households share
sections.summary: In 2020, 52.5% of married households were dual-income, up from 47.1% in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2020, 52.5% of married households were dual-income households, an increase from 47.1% in 2010.

sections.label: Gender-neutral divorce maintenance debate
sections.summary: A Minister said the maintenance regime protects financially vulnerable parties, and a Member urged the Government to reconsider gender-neutral divorce maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What is important are the roles assumed in the marriage." In the 2022 debate on amendments to the Women’s Charter, the Minister of State for Social and Family Development responded to calls to provide maintenance to husbands by stating that the purpose of the current regime is to protect parties who tend to be more financially vulnerable post-divorce, that is, women and incapacitated men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, this does not stop the Government from extending the safeguards provided by the maintenance regime to another potentially vulnerable group, namely, stay-at-home husbands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even in a gender-neutral maintenance regime, any maintenance to spouses would be awarded at the Court’s discretion and such a regime should not disadvantage vulnerable women who can still be awarded maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In summary, Mr Deputy Speaker, Sir, I urge the Government to reconsider making maintenance in cases of divorce gender-neutral.

sections.label: Maintenance Enforcement Officers recruitment numbers
sections.summary: The Member asked how many Maintenance Enforcement Officers the Courts expect the Ministry to recruit for the high volume of maintenance summons applications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Take the incoming Maintenance Enforcement Officers (MEOs), for example.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How many of these MEOs will the Courts be expecting for the Ministry to recruit in order to cope with the high volume of maintenance summons applications?

sections.label: Docket system for divorce cases
sections.summary: The Member sought clarification on whether a specific judge would be assigned to a divorce case from commencement to conclusion under the ordinary route.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to seek clarification on whether this would mean a docket system where a specific judge is assigned to a case right from the beginning when a divorce is commenced under the ordinary route to oversee the case through to its conclusion.

sections.label: Strengthening Family Therapeutic Justice
sections.summary: The Member expressed confidence that MinLaw, MSF and the Family Justice Court will assure the public of benefits from these rights and supported strengthening Family Therapeutic Justice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Although it is difficult to judge people's family affairs, I am confident that MinLaw and MSF and the Family Justice Court will assure the public how these rights can further reduce unnecessary legal proceedings, alleviate the mental and financial stress faced by the parties in divorce proceedings, improve broken family relationships due to divorce, and minimise the intentional or unintentional psychological harm done to the children by either party during this period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Strengthening Family Therapeutic Justice presents us with an opportunity to create a more compassionate and effective family law system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: By embracing this approach, we can reduce the acrimony, ensure fairer outcomes and prioritise the best interests of our children.

sections.label: Support for Maintenance Enforcement Officers
sections.summary: The Member said the current situation is unfair to maintenance applicants and supported amendments allowing appointment of Maintenance Enforcement Officers for more sustainable maintenance outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This is unfair to an applicant who has been granted the maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, Sir, I support the amendments to the Women’s Charter to allow the appointment of the Maintenance Enforcement Officers (MEO) in order to have a more sustainable maintenance outcome.

sections.label: Court powers for maintenance enforcement
sections.summary: Courts should act expeditiously and make interim orders so financially stretched applicants receive maintenance, and attach salary or assets when respondents deliberately refuse payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In particular, the Courts should be given the powers to act expeditiously and to make interim orders, whenever necessary, to ensure that complainants or applicants who are financially stretched are able to receive the maintenance that they deserve and are entitled to receive; otherwise, the applicant would typically suffer and situations where there are children involved will result in hardship for the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Where the MEOs are able to ascertain that the respondent is deliberately refusing to make the maintenance payment, the Court should not hesitate to attach the salary of the respondent or attach his assets in order to enforce the maintenance order.

sections.label: Support for Maintenance Enforcement Process Bill
sections.summary: Subject to clarifications, the speaker supports the Bill, whose officers form a new Maintenance Enforcement Process simplifying applications on non-payment of maintenance orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Subject to the above clarifications, Sir, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The officers are part of a new Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP), which will simplify applications related to non-payment of maintenance orders.

sections.label: Prioritising respondents and rebuttable presumption
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the MEO or Court prioritises when a sole breadwinner's income is insufficient, and supports a rebuttable presumption on respondents dissipating assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: How would the MEO or Court prioritise if the respondent who is the only sole breadwinner and also child who needs to support parents and his income is insufficient to support all, especially if the parents are sick?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am supportive of the introduction of "rebuttable presumption" to address the issue of respondents dissipating assets, such as by spending money or moving it to another account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The applicant must show that this happened less than three years before he or she applied for a clawback order, or that there is an impending move that would frustrate enforcement of the maintenance order.

sections.label: MEO seeking third-party information
sections.summary: The new section 86 allows the Maintenance Enforcement Officer to seek Court orders for banks or prescribed third parties to provide information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the new section 86 allows the Maintenance Enforcement Officer (MEO) to seek Court orders for banks or prescribed third parties to provide information.

sections.label: MEO conciliation sessions
sections.summary: The new section 88 allows an MEO to conduct conciliation sessions to help both parties agree on maintenance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, the new section 88 allows an MEO to conduct conciliation sessions to help both parties agree on maintenance.

sections.label: Court-ordered financial counselling
sections.summary: The new section 91(b) gives the Court powers to order a party to undergo financial counselling as part of maintenance enforcement proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 91(b) makes progress in this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It provides the Court with powers to order a party to undergo financial counselling as part of maintenance enforcement proceedings.

sections.label: Child's wishes in Court
sections.summary: A key Women's Charter amendment covers the scenario where the Court considers the child's wishes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: One of the key amendments to the Women’s Charter will cater to the scenario when the wishes of the child are to be considered by the Court.

sections.label: Maintenance Enforcement Process enhancements
sections.summary: The speaker supports proposed enhancements to the Maintenance Enforcement Process to differentiate those unable to pay from those who refuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Next, I support the proposed enhancements to the Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP), which will help to differentiate between those who are unable to pay maintenance and those who refuse to pay.

sections.label: Conciliation by Maintenance Enforcement Officers
sections.summary: Under the MEP, the existing mediation process will be replaced by conciliation by a new unit of Maintenance Enforcement Officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Under the MEP, the existing mediation process will be replaced by a conciliation process undertaken by this newly established unit of Maintenance Enforcement Officers (MEOs).

sections.label: Women's Charter maintenance amendments
sections.summary: The Bill amends section 71 to allow attachment of earning orders and adds section 81 on maintenance enforcement orders including Show-Payment Orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the Bill, amendments are proposed to the Women's Charter in section 71 to empower the Court to make attachment of earning order for maintenance to secure payment of any maintenance from the respondent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Bill added a new section 81 to the Women's Charter to provide directions to the Court on the orders that it may or must make on a maintenance enforcement application, which included a Show-Payment Order and, when breached, the respondent is liable for imprisonment.

sections.label: Divorcee's unpaid maintenance order
sections.summary: After her divorce, the Court ordered her former husband to pay about $1,200 monthly maintenance, which he has not paid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Following her divorce a couple of years ago, while the Court has ordered her former husband to pay about $1,200 monthly maintenance to her and their three children, he has not done so.

sections.label: Warrant of arrest uncontactable ex-husband
sections.summary: The Court issued a warrant of arrest but her ex-husband was not contactable, so the alimony could not be claimed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the process of claiming maintenance, the Court issued a warrant of arrest but Mdm Goh's ex-husband was not contactable, hence, the alimony could not be claimed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Her story illustrated the importance of therapeutic justice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that MinLaw and MSF will provide more social assistance in cases, such as Mdm Goh's, and to help them claim maintenance.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill despite the considerations raised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the considerations that I have raised, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

sections.label: Appellate Court share ruling
sections.summary: The appellate Court held she had a share and interest in the flat though not listed as owner, and she received outstanding maintenance after a lengthy Court process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Eventually, the appellate Court held that she had a share and interest in the flat, notwithstanding that she was not listed as an owner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: She also received settlement of the outstanding maintenance owed from the ex-spouse, but this was not before enduring a lengthy Court process.

sections.label: MEP awareness and Syariah orders
sections.summary: The speaker asks what steps MinLaw and MSF will take on MEP awareness and assistance, and hopes the MEP applies equally to Syariah Court orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Lastly, what are the steps that MinLaw, together with MSF, will take to raise awareness of the MEP and render assistance to laypersons who do not know how to navigate the claims and applications?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also hope that the MEP will also apply equally for the enforcement of Syariah Court orders, especially on maintenance-like orders on payment of nafkah iddah and mutaah.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In the past, as I had shared earlier in the case of Mdm Wati, not her real name, the process of receiving her child's maintenance not only took a long time, but it was also mentally exhausting and left her feeling dispirited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: When a marriage ends, the couple should separate amicably, because even though they are no longer a family, the family ties and the love between the parents and their children should never cease to exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope, with this new process, we can ensure that the child's maintenance can be provisioned as soon as possible and the responsibility of providing maintenance as a parent can be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In English): Sir, notwithstanding my clarifications and suggestions, I stand fully in support of the Bill.

sections.label: MEP and Syariah Court orders
sections.summary: The MEP will apply to Syariah Court orders which under the Administration of Muslim Law Act may be treated as Family Court maintenance orders for enforcement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The MEP will, indeed, apply to orders made by the Syariah Court which, under the Administration of Muslim Law Act, may be treated as maintenance orders made by the Family Court for the purposes of enforcement.

sections.label: Three-year enforcement deadline
sections.summary: An applicant generally needs to commence proceedings to enforce arrears within three years from when the arrears are due.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Generally, an applicant needs to commence proceedings to enforce arrears within three years from the time that such arrears are due.

sections.label: Agencies listed in opening speech
sections.summary: In Minister Shanmugam's opening speech, he listed the CDP and Government agencies such as CPF Board, HDB, IRAS, SLA and LTA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: In Minister Shanmugam’s opening speech, he listed them: the CDP and Government agencies, such as CPF Board, HDB, IRAS, SLA and LTA.

sections.label: MEO final report submission
sections.summary: The MEO's final report will be given to both parties and submitted to the Court.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The MEO’s final report will be provided to both parties and submitted to the Court.

sections.label: Respondent means to pay maintenance
sections.summary: Mr Gan and Mr Lim Biow Chuan cited respondents able to earn but choosing not to, and there is no fixed formula for means to pay maintenance.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Both Mr Gan and Mr Lim Biow Chuan cited examples of respondents who have the ability to earn an income or better income but chose not to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: There is no fixed formula to determine whether a respondent has the means to pay maintenance.

sections.label: MEP and variation of maintenance orders
sections.summary: The MEP does not change substantive law on varying maintenance orders; the Court may vary an order for misrepresentation, mistake of fact, or material change in circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The MEP does not change the substantive law in relation to variation of maintenance orders: the test that the respondent has to satisfy remains the same.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For example, the Court may vary a maintenance order made during matrimonial proceedings only when it is satisfied that: the order was based on any misrepresentation or mistake of fact; or where there has been any material change in circumstances.

sections.label: Attachment of earnings and gig work
sections.summary: Mr Ng asked whether freelance or gig economy earnings may be attached; earnings are defined in new section 76 of the Women's Charter as wages or salary under a contract of service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: On attachment of earnings orders, Mr Ng asked whether earnings from freelance or gig economy work are earnings that may be attached. "Earnings" for the purpose of attachment of earnings orders is defined in the new section 76 of the Women's Charter to refer to wages or salary payable under a contract of service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Therefore, depending on the way the contractual relationship between the worker and the firm is structured, it may well be that, in some cases, such earnings may fall within the definition of "earnings".

sections.label: Gig work attachment of earnings orders
sections.summary: Including such arrangements may cause hardship and administrative challenges, so attachment of earnings orders will generally not be made for unstable gig work income.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Including such arrangements may lead to hardship for the parties and administrative challenges for the firms who engage these workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Hence, attachment of earnings orders will, generally, not be made in respect of income from gig work, which is unstable.

sections.label: MEOs verify financial difficulties
sections.summary: The MEOs can verify genuine financial difficulties and may refer parties to Social Service Offices for financial assistance or other support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The MEOs will be able to verify whether the respondent has genuine financial difficulties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Where the respondent has genuine financial difficulties, the MEOs, where appropriate, may refer the parties to Social Service Offices for financial assistance or other forms of support.

sections.label: Training social service officers
sections.summary: MSF will explore Ms Ng's suggestion to train social service officers and social workers to help vulnerable clients with online applications and referrals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Ms Ng's suggestion to train social service officers and social workers to help their vulnerable clients navigate the online application process and make the appropriate referrals, is a good one, which MSF will explore.

sections.label: Mandatory Co-Parenting Programme
sections.summary: All divorcing parents with minor children must go through the Mandatory Co-Parenting Programme before filing for divorce.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Mandatory Co-Parenting Programme, which all divorcing parents with minor children must go through before filing for divorce, will equip and encourage parents to make informed decisions, including on post-divorce housing arrangements, which prioritise the well-being of their children.

sections.label: Bill recommendations on judicial powers
sections.summary: The Bill recommends strengthening judges' powers, authorising judges to prohibit unnecessary applications, and enabling restrictions on cross-examination.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The recommendations in this Bill include: (a) Strengthening the power of judges to take a proactive approach to the cases before them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This includes allowing them to make certain orders at their own discretion to address any urgent need of the families involved; (b) Authorising the judge to prohibit the parties involved from submitting additional applications which are unnecessary and have no strong justifications, without the leave of the Court; and (c) Enabling judges to impose restrictions on cross-examination under certain circumstances, where the questioning of a vulnerable witness may be intimidating or oppressive.

sections.label: Maintenance Enforcement Officers unit
sections.summary: A new unit of Maintenance Enforcement Officers will be set up and the Maintenance Enforcement Process will apply to certain Syariah Court orders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: A new unit of Maintenance Enforcement Officers (MEO) will be set up.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: MEO will be authorised to obtain the information directly from the parties involved or from designated entities, such as banks, CPF Board, HDB, IRAS, SLA, LTA and CDP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: The Maintenance Enforcement Process (MEP) will apply to Court orders made by the Singapore Syariah Court which, under the Administration of Muslim Law Act (AMLA), may be treated as maintenance orders made by the Family Court for the purposes of enforcement.

sections.label: Reducing financial neglect
sections.summary: The new MEP is hoped to reduce situations where children and vulnerable family members are left in financial neglect.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: With the new MEP strengthening deterrence against respondents who refuse to pay, and facilitating more sustainable maintenance outcomes where respondents cannot pay, it is hoped that situations where children and vulnerable family members are left in financial neglect will be reduced.

sections.label: Family Assist portal launch
sections.summary: In December 2021, MSF launched the Family Assist portal to support couples contemplating divorce and provide information and services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In December 2021, MSF launched the Family Assist portal which supports couples contemplating divorce and provides them with information and services to make informed decisions in the best interest of their children.

sections.label: Data sharing with SSOs
sections.summary: Data sharing between the Maintenance Enforcement Process and the SSOs will be streamlined where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Where possible, we will streamline the sharing of data between the Maintenance Enforcement Process and the SSOs.

sections.label: Men applying for maintenance
sections.summary: In 2016 men could apply for maintenance if incapacitated, unable to earn a livelihood, and unable to support themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In 2016, we took a significant step to allow men to apply for maintenance if they were (a) incapacitated before or during the course of the marriage; (b) are unable to earn a livelihood; and (c) are unable to support themselves.

sections.label: Family violence and maintenance review
sections.summary: MSF will study whether husbands and ex-husbands can apply for maintenance, and a Family Violence (Amendment) Bill will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: MSF will continue to study the issue and review if husbands and ex-husbands can apply for maintenance payments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Queries were also raised by Members regarding support for family violence survivors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: I will be introducing the Family Violence (Amendment) Bill tomorrow in this House, which will effect the key recommendations from the Taskforce on Family Violence in tackling family violence.

sections.label: MEP implementation and MEOs
sections.summary: The MEP will take time to implement to ensure the right MEOs are hired and the process is set up well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The MEP will take some time to be implemented, as we want to ensure that the right persons are hired to play the key role of MEOs and that the process is set up well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: My colleagues Senior Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu Mahzam and Minister of State Sun Xueling have answered the points raised by Members.
